main_issue: Who should clean the shellfish-contaminated shared pan tonight so Agent D (allergic) can cook, and what kitchen rule should apply going forward

A-B.evidence: A pushes everyone to clean together (T20, T22); B refuses: 'I'm not cleaning a mess I didn't make' (T23); A challenges B's double standard (T26).

A-C.evidence: A accuses C (T9) but then A objects to D cleaning (T16) and proposes a firm rule (T20), matching C's rule and objection (T3, T18, T24).

A-D.evidence: A wants D able to cook but says the user should clean and objects to D cleaning (T16); D keeps saying 'I'll just clean it' (T15, T25).

B-C.evidence: B says 'Let's just move on' (T17); C replies that moving on means it keeps happening (T18) and criticizes the stalemate (T24).

B-D.evidence: B accepts D's offer to clean ('He offered to do it', T17); D ends up cleaning it himself (T25), which fits B's preference, though D did not endorse B's stance.

C-D.evidence: C backs D's need to cook and the cleaning rule (T3, T14); D agrees ('He's right', T19), but D still plans to clean it himself (T25), against C's objection (T18, T24).
